book_title: Inside the Five-Engine Machine: From ₹20 Trades to ₹4,351 Crore Margin Books
question: How does Groww actually make money across its five operating verticals, and how fast is it reducing its reliance on equity derivatives?

epigraph.quote: A brokerage that only clips ₹20 tickets is a utility; a platform that owns the asset, the margin book, and the advice becomes a franchise.
epigraph.author: Financial Services Underwriting Note

web_blocks.html: Groww operates as a multi-vertical digital financial ecosystem under Billionbrains Garage Ventures Limited and its specialized subsidiaries: Groww Invest Tech Private Limited (stockbroking & depository), Groww Creditserv Technology Private Limited (NBFC lending), Groww Asset Management Limited (mutual fund manufacturing), Finwizard Technology / Fisdom (wealth advisory, PMS, AIF), Groww Insurance Broking, and Groww Pay Services [10, 11, 12]. Crucially. Meanwhile, equity derivatives remain the single largest revenue contributor, management has deliberately engineered a 12.2 percentage point reduction in derivatives concentration over the past year—from 56.9% of total income in Q2 FY26 down to 44.8% in Q2 FY27 [14].

web_blocks.title: Deep Dive: 915 by Groww and the Pro-Trader Ring-Fence

web_blocks.html: A classic product dilemma in retail fintech is that tools built for active options scalpers overwhelm long-term SIP investors. Meanwhile, minimalist investing apps lose power traders to specialized terminals. Groww solved this by launching 915 by Groww—a standalone high-performance terminal and mobile interface built exclusively for active F&O traders [15]. It features live Open Interest (OI) shifts, option Greeks, multi-leg basket order execution, customizable workspaces, and a dedicated 'Scalper Zone' [15]. This separation allowed Groww to expand its retail equity derivatives premium ADTO market share from 8.6% in Q2 FY26 to 11.0% in Q2 FY27 [19] without compromising the simplicity of its flagship mass-market app.

web_blocks.title: Deep Dive: Why MTF and Wealth Are Changing the Earnings Quality

web_blocks.html: The most important structural shift inside Groww's P&L is the rapid rise of interest-yielding balance-sheet assets alongside traditional ₹20 transaction tickets. In Q2 FY27, Groww's MTF net book reached ₹4,351 crore—growing by roughly ₹600–700 crore per quarter and expanding 161% YoY [14]. Unlike options brokerage. This resets to zero every morning and depends on daily volatility, an MTF book generates recurring daily interest income as long as positions remain open. Even at 2.7% industry MTF market share (up from 1.6% YoY) [19], Groww has substantial runway to cross-sell margin funding to its 1.35 crore active equity clients. Simultaneously, Groww Creditserv extends Loans Against Mutual Funds (LAMF) to the massive base of SIP holders sitting on ₹3.87 trillion of total customer assets [6, 12], monetizing long-term buy-and-hold investors who never trade F&O.

On the affluent end, the $150 million all-cash Fisdom acquisition bridges a historical graduation leak [10]. Groww's core app excelled at ₹5,000 SIPs and ₹20 trades. But struggled to retain users once their portfolios crossed ₹50 lakh–₹5 crore and required tax harvesting, PMS, AIFs, or human-assisted fixed-income planning. Combining Fisdom's advisory stack and regional bank partnerships with Groww's digital distribution pushed Wealth AUM past ₹10,000 crore in Q2 FY27, while Groww AMC more than doubled its AUM to ₹7,179 crore (from ₹2,928 crore YoY) across index, active equity, and debt schemes [4].

Beyond transaction fees, Groww's multi-product architecture creates a compounding cross-sell flywheel that traditional single-line brokers cannot replicate [1][6]. A salaried engineer in Pune who starts a ₹5,000 monthly SIP in a direct Nifty 50 index fund costs Groww virtually zero incremental marketing rupees to onboard onto equities, IPO applications, or MTF when her investable surplus grows. In Q2 FY27, Groww's active client base of ~1.35 crore generated rising multi-product penetration across Cash Equities, Equity Derivatives, MTF, Personal Loans (via Groww Creditserv), Commodities, and Wealth Management (Fisdom), lifting overall blended monetization even as pure F&O volumes normalized [6][8].

Quantifying the cross-sell progression across cohorts makes the flywheel concrete: new users onboarded via zero-fee direct mutual funds or IPOs typically show modest first-year revenue per user. But by Year 2 and Year 3 a rising fraction activates equity delivery, MTF, and commodities [6][8]. Because Groww's incremental cost to serve an existing KYC-verified user is negligible, every rupee of incremental MTF interest or wealth advisory fee flows through at exceptionally high marginal contribution.
This mix shift is key. Less reliance on F&O lowers risk. More MTF and wealth fees add steady income.

book_paragraphs: When you open Groww's income statement, it is tempting to think of the company as a simple digital tollbooth charging ₹20 every time a retail trader clicks 'Buy' or 'Sell.' That used to be mostly true. Today, it is only half the story.
To see what Groww actually is in late 2026, walk through five real-world customers using the platform on the same Tuesday morning.

Customer one is a 26-year-old software engineer in Indore. She opens Groww once a month to check her ₹5,000 systematic investment plan in a direct-plan index fund. Groww earns zero rupees on that SIP. It looks like charity—until you notice she also applied for an IPO through Groww's UPI mandate this week (part of 42 lakh users who gave Groww a 22% share of all retail IPO allotments in Q2 FY27) and bought ₹30,000 of cash equities, paying a ₹20 ticket. Across India, Groww now commands 14.8% of all mutual fund SIP inflows and 15.4% of retail cash equity turnover.

Customer two is an active options trader in Pune. He doesn't even use the main Groww app anymore; he logs into '915 by Groww,' a stripped-down, high-speed terminal built specifically for derivatives scalpers, complete with live open-interest shifts, option Greeks, multi-leg basket orders, and a Scalper Zone. He fires off a four-leg Nifty iron condor and pays ₹20 per leg. Equity derivatives still represent the single biggest slice of Groww's pie—44.8% of total income in Q2 FY27—but notice the direction of travel: just twelve months earlier, derivatives were 56.9% of total income. That 12.2 percentage point drop in concentration did not happen by accident.

Customer three explains why. Picture a swing trader in Bengaluru who spots a breakout in a mid-cap industrial stock. She has ₹4 lakh in cash or pledged shares, and uses Groww's Margin Trading Facility (MTF) to buy an ₹8 lakh delivery position for thirty days. Groww's broking arm funds the other ₹4 lakh and charges daily interest. Because MTF earns interest every calendar day a position stays open—rather than relying on frantic intraday turnover—it has become Groww's fastest-scaling engine. Its net MTF book surged 161% year-on-year to ₹4,351 crore in Q2 FY27, adding ₹600 to ₹700 crore every single quarter, while its MTF market share climbed from 1.6% to 2.7%.

Customer four is an affluent business owner in Ahmedabad whose mutual fund portfolio has grown past ₹2 crore. Historically, this is the exact moment a discount broker lost its best customer to a private bank wealth manager. Groww plugged that graduation leak by buying Fisdom for $150 million in cash, integrating PMS, AIFs, and human-assisted advisory under its 'W' wealth desk, which has already crossed ₹10,000 crore in assets—alongside ₹7,179 crore inside Groww's own mutual fund AMC.

Finally, customer five is a commodity trader in Surat hedging gold mini futures on MCX in the evening, or a SIP holder tapping Groww Creditserv (the in-house NBFC) for an instant loan against mutual funds without selling her compounding portfolio. Five engines, one shared customer ledger—and every new engine makes the core ₹20 brokerage ticket less of a single point of failure.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The single most encouraging number in Chapter 2 is not the 47% revenue growth—it is the 12.2 percentage point drop in equity derivatives concentration (from 56.9% to 44.8%) in a single year while operating margins expanded.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through Every Revenue Engine Through a Real Customer's Eyes
paragraphs: Let us step inside the Groww app as an actual customer so the segment numbers come alive. Imagine Priya, a 29-year-old software engineer in Bengaluru earning ₹18 lakh a year. Her journey begins in Groww's zero-commission Direct Mutual Fund and IPO funnel—she sets up a ₹10,000 monthly SIP in three minutes using UPI AutoPay. On this entry product, Groww earns zero trail commission, which is why legacy distributors once dismissed Groww as unmonetizable.

Six months later, Priya notices a mid-cap stock she follows and buys ₹50,000 worth of shares in Cash Equities. Now she pays Groww's flat brokerage and exchange-linked transaction fees. A year later, she experiments with Margin Trading Facility (MTF), putting down ₹1 lakh of her own cash and borrowing ₹2 lakh from Groww at ~14%–15% annualized interest to hold a swing position—instantly generating high-margin net interest income for Groww. If she later needs liquidity for a home down payment, Groww Creditserv offers a pre-approved personal loan or loan against mutual funds. And as her portfolio crosses ₹25 lakh, Groww's Fisdom wealth arm steps in with curated advisory and fixed-income products.

That single-customer lifecycle explains why Groww's revenue mix is shifting so rapidly. In Q2 FY26, equity derivatives accounted for 56.9 percent of total income—a classic vulnerability if regulators curb retail options. By Q2 FY27, derivatives share had fallen 12.2 percentage points to 44.8 percent, even as total revenue surged, because MTF, cash equities, wealth management, and Groww AMC scaled right alongside it.

book_subsections.title: Segment Economics: Comparing Transaction Velocity vs. Annuity Assets
paragraphs: Let us organize Groww's business lines into two mental buckets so you can weigh their durability properly: high-velocity transaction engines and sticky annuity engines. Equity derivatives and cash equities sit in the transaction bucket. They generate extraordinary cash flow when retail sentiment is buoyant, but turnover can dip 15 to 25 percent during sideways or fearful markets—or whenever SEBI raises contract lot sizes.

In the annuity and asset-backed bucket sit Groww's Margin Trading Facility (₹4,351 crore net book), Groww Mutual Fund (₹7,179 crore AUM), Fisdom Wealth Management (over ₹10,000 crore AUM), and Groww Creditserv's secured lending products. Unlike a one-off options trade, an MTF balance earns daily interest as long as the investor holds the stock, and a mutual fund SIP or wealth mandate compounds alongside India's nominal GDP. Watching the annuity bucket grow faster than the transaction bucket is the single cleanest indicator that Groww's business quality is improving every quarter.

book_subsections.title: Why Fisdom and Groww AMC Complete the Wealth Lifecycle
paragraphs: Before we leave the segment breakdown, let us look closely at why acquiring Indiabulls AMC (now Groww Mutual Fund) for ₹175.6 crore and integrating Fisdom Wealth Management matter so much over a five-year horizon. In pure broking, you only earn when a customer clicks Buy or Sell. In asset management and wealth advisory, you earn a steady basis-point fee on every rupee of assets sitting on the platform—even when the customer goes on vacation for six months.

Groww AMC has already scaled to ₹7,179 crore in AUM by launching low-cost passive index funds and ETFs tailored to its retail user base, while Fisdom brings over ₹10,000 crore in wealth AUM and high-net-worth distribution capabilities. Together, they ensure that as Groww's 24.3 million transacting users mature from ₹50,000 portfolios into ₹25 lakh and ₹1 crore portfolios, they never outgrow the Groww ecosystem.
